newsitem.title: USA: American Express Q2 paced by fund unit.
newsitem.headline: American Express Q2 paced by fund unit.

text.p: Second-quarter net income at American Express Co was paced by the American Express Financial Advisors (AEFA) unit, where net income rose to $183 million from $153 million, an increase of 20 percent.

In the first quarter of 1997 AEFA had net income of $157 million. AEFA had record sales of mutual funds in the second quarter -- $4.09 billion versus $3.76 billion in the same quarter a year ago and $4.03 billion in the first quarter.
Travel Related Services (TRS), the company's biggest unit, reported net income rose to $355 million from $322 million a year ago, an increase of 10 percent.
In the first quarter of 1997 net income in the TRS unit was $315 million.

Revenue in the TRS unit rose to $3.15 billion from $2.93 billion a year ago and $2.97 billion in the first quarter of 1997. The year-over-year percentage increase was seven percent. Excluding the impact of securitizing a portion of charge card portfolios and a reduction in investments related to consolidations, revenue rose nine percent from a year ago.
American Express said growth in TRS revenue reflected higher worldwide billed business and growth in cardmember loans.
American Express said improvement in billed business reflected a greater number of cards outstanding and higher spending per cardmember.

Average spending per basic cardmember was $1,602 in the second quarter, compared with $1,545 a year ago and $1,498 in the first quarter. Total cards in force worldwide were 42.3 million in the second quarter versus 39.3 million a year ago.
Total billed business worldwide was $51.9 billion in the second quarter compared with $45.8 billion a year ago and $47.9 billion in the first quarter.

Credit trends were essentially steady. The loss provision overalll on a managed asset basis rose to $537 million from $466 million a year ago and $498 million in the first quarter. The loss provision in the lending category was $203 million cmopared with $138 million a year ago and $222 million in the first quarter.
The increase in the provision from a year ago reflected both higher outstanding loans and loss rates.
In owned and managed U.S. cardmember lending, 2.5 percnet of loans were past due 30-89 days versus 2.3 percent a year ago and 2.6 percent in the first quarter of 1997.
In owned and managed U.S. cardmember lending, 1.1 percnet of loans were past due 90 days or more versus 0.9 percent a year ago and 1.0 percent in the first quarter of 1997.

Average loans were $13.2 billion in the second quarter, compared with $10.5 billion a year ago and $12.8 billion in the first quarter. The net write-off rate was 6.0 percent in the first quarter versus 5.2 percent a year ago and 5.1 percent in the first quarter.
Susan Roth, Donaldson, Lufkin & Jenrette Securities Corp analyst, said the quarter was better than she expected. She said it was a "clean" quarter for credit quality.
